idiom_name: for (x <- xs) desugaring to foreach/map/flatMap, plus collection messages
implementation_notes: In Scala a for expression is notation over messages: for (x <- xs) body becomes xs.foreach(x => body), for (x <- xs) yield f(x) becomes xs.map(f), and guards or extra generators become withFilter and flatMap - so any type implementing those methods is enumerable with the same syntax and the pattern's 'one message' is literally the method call. Collections offer the transforming messages directly (map/filter/foldLeft/collect/partition), the lazy variants hang off Iterator/View/LazyList so intermediate collections are not materialised, and pattern-matching generators traverse maps and tuples cleanly. A while loop over indices is reserved for genuine mutation or performance-critical code.
code_sketch:
for (line <- order.lines) applyDiscount(line, policy)     // => foreach

for (line <- order.lines if line.taxable) yield line.amount   // withFilter+map
val total = order.lines.iterator.map(_.amount).sum        // lazy Iterator walk

order.lines.foreach { case Line(sku, amount) => audit(sku, amount) }
pitfalls: A for without yield desugars to foreach and returns Unit, so a comprehension that forgot yield silently discards the mapped values.

Mixing lazy and strict collections in one comprehension changes when work happens (LazyList/Iterator defer, List does not), and an Iterator-based for is consumed once - a second traversal sees an empty collection.

Scala 2 collections are not fail-fast: mutating a mutable collection during traversal is unchecked (no ConcurrentModificationException) and produces silent skips or repeats, so prefer immutable collections.
